authority: Planner definitions for consistent original authoring; not quoted official definitions or current policy/medical guidance.

entries.meaning: Improvement in people's quality of life across economic, social, political and environmental dimensions.
Development that meets present needs without undermining future generations' ability to meet their own needs.
The value of final output attributable to a country's residents over a period, including net income from abroad. Distinguish the national total from a per-person figure.
GNP divided by the population; an average that does not show how income is distributed.
A composite measure combining health, education and income dimensions of human development; it does not capture every aspect of development.
A measure of overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards; it differs from an income-only poverty measure.
A measurable feature used as evidence about a wider condition; one indicator seldom gives a complete account of development.
The creation of goods and services that satisfy needs and wants.
Something essential for basic survival or well-being, such as adequate food, safe water or shelter.
Something a person would like beyond what is essential for basic survival or well-being.
Natural resources used in production, including physical space, water, minerals and soil.
Human physical and mental effort used in production.
Finance available to acquire resources for production; distinguish it from the productive equipment purchased.
Produced assets used to make other goods and services, such as tools, machinery and buildings.
Organising productive resources and undertaking the decisions and risks involved in production.
Splitting production into specialised tasks carried out by different workers.
Concentrating on a narrower range of tasks or products to develop skills or efficiency.
Reductions in average cost associated with operating at a larger scale, where the relevant efficiencies are achieved.
Technology suited to the local purpose, resources, skills, costs and environmental conditions; it need not be the most complex option.
Production that relies relatively heavily on labour compared with capital equipment.
Production that relies relatively heavily on capital equipment compared with labour.
Growth in the importance and capacity of industrial production within an economy.
Developing domestic production to replace goods previously imported.
Producing goods or services primarily for sale in foreign markets.
Transferring ownership of an enterprise or asset from the state to private owners.
An increase in the proportion of a population living in urban areas; distinguish it from an increase in urban population alone.
The situation of people without work who are available for and seeking work; exact statistical definitions depend on the source.
Having work that uses less than a person's available working time or productive capacity; it differs from having no work.
Economic activity operating outside some formal registration or regulatory arrangements; it is not the same concept as an informal settlement.
Growing a single crop over an area, often repeatedly; distinguish it from rotating different crops.
Growing different crops in a planned sequence on the same land over time.
Equal rights, opportunities and treatment regardless of gender; formal equality does not by itself establish equal lived outcomes.
The number of people per unit area, commonly people per square kilometre.
The spatial pattern showing where people live and how they are spread across an area.
Live births during a year per thousand people in the population.
Deaths during a year per thousand people in the population in the crude measure used here.
Deaths before the first birthday per thousand live births, for a stated period.
The average number of years a person at a stated age is expected to live under the mortality conditions used in the estimate.
A diagram showing the age and sex composition of a population, with the unit and date stated.
Learning rooted in a community's inherited knowledge, practices and values; this classification differs from formal versus non-formal provision.
Education organised within the recognised, structured education system, normally with planned stages and qualifications.
Learning through everyday experience and interaction outside a planned education programme.
Organised learning outside the main formal education system, such as a planned adult skills programme.
The fundamental rules establishing how a state is organised, how public power is exercised and the rights recognised.
Recognised legitimacy to make decisions or exercise power within a specified role.
The capacity to influence actions or outcomes; it can exist without recognised legitimate authority.
The value of goods exported minus the value of goods imported over a stated period. State when a dataset includes services as well.
A record of economic transactions between a country's residents and the rest of the world over a period; it is broader than trade in goods.
Increasing connections and interdependence across countries through flows such as trade, investment, information and people.
Investment by an investor based in another country that establishes a lasting interest and influence in an enterprise.
Assistance provided to support relief or development, in forms such as finance, goods, services or technical expertise.
Aid provided directly from one country to another.
Aid provided through an organisation supported by multiple countries.
Aid carrying conditions that restrict how it is used, such as requiring purchases from the donor.
Money advanced under an agreement requiring repayment, often with interest.
An outstanding obligation to repay borrowed money; distinguish the original loan from the remaining amount owed.
A broad statement of what an enquiry intends to find out, linked to its research question or hypothesis.
A specific task or target that helps the enquiry achieve its aim.
A tentative, testable statement about a relationship or outcome that evidence can support or challenge.
A focused question that the enquiry seeks to answer using evidence.
Data collected first-hand for the present enquiry.
Data already collected or published for another purpose and used in the present enquiry.
A small preliminary trial of research procedures or instruments used to identify problems and make improvements before the main enquiry.
The whole group of units or people that the enquiry is intended to investigate.
The selected subset of the research population from which data are collected.
Selecting units by a chance procedure so each member of the defined research population has an equal chance of selection; convenience selection does not meet that rule.
Dividing a population into relevant groups and selecting from each group, using an explicit selection method.
Selecting units at a fixed interval from an ordered list after an appropriate starting point.
An observed result or pattern established from the collected evidence.
An evidence-based answer to the research question or judgement about the hypothesis, within the enquiry's limits.
A proposed feasible action linked to the findings and conclusions, identifying who could implement it.
A company operating productive activities in more than one country; distinguish its international operations from merely exporting goods.
Development initiated with active participation by local people around their own priorities and resources, rather than solely directed from above.

Abandoning an infant, commonly a newborn, in circumstances that leave the infant without appropriate care. Discuss the development issue sensitively without stereotypes or requests for personal disclosure.
A good or service sold to a buyer in another country.
A good or service bought from a supplier in another country.
Movement of people from rural places to urban places to live; it is one contributor to urbanisation, not its definition.
Farming primarily to meet the needs of the farming household rather than primarily for sale.

A syllabus category describing a country undergoing substantial industrial expansion and structural change; named syllabus examples are historical illustrations, not claims of a current official classification.

Less economically developed country and more economically developed country: broad comparative syllabus categories that require specified development indicators and do not describe every household within a country.
Technology between very simple and highly complex forms, often designed to use accessible skills and resources. Whether it is appropriate depends on the local purpose and conditions.
An organisation owned and operated jointly by members to meet shared economic or social needs.
Basic essential health services and preventive support made accessible within communities; teach the development and service-provision principle without clinical treatment advice.
The share of a defined population meeting the stated reading-and-writing criterion; comparisons require the same age range, definition and period.

A simplified model linking changes in birth and death rates to population growth during development. Teach the broad syllabus relationship without adding extra stages or treating every country as following an identical timetable.

Education shaped by contemporary institutions and knowledge, including formal systems; distinguish this broad contrast with traditional education from the separate formal/informal/non-formal classification.
